anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Inaccurate, stale, or missing optimizer statistics lead to systematic cardinality misestimates.
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer’s choice-of-plan logic produces a sub-optimal execution plan even when statistics are otherwise acceptable.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : The physical storage layer cannot supply reads or absorb writes at the rate demanded, saturating I/O bandwidth, IOPS, or latency budgets.

Composite definition: The database simultaneously suffers from (1) misleading optimizer statistics, (2) poor plan-selection logic or plan reuse, and (3) a saturated storage subsystem. The combination yields execution plans that are both logically inappropriate and physically starved for I/O capacity, driving severe and unpredictable performance degradation.

Combined phenomena: • Estimates versus actual row counts diverge wildly while the plan cache shows frequent plan flips, hinting at both statistics and decision-logic instability. • Queries oscillate between parallel-scan, serial full-scan, and poorly-parameterized index paths, each generating excessive physical I/O that collides with already maxed-out storage queues. • Wait profiles show a mix of optimizer-related recompiles, "bad plan" symptoms (nested-loop blow-outs, hash spill to temp), and chronic FILEIO/IO_COMPLETION waits; CPU stays moderate but response times spike. • Bulk-load or ETL windows trigger immediate plan regression followed by device-level read/write latency explosions, elongating both OLTP and analytics workloads. • DBA attempts to force plans or update statistics give only transient relief because the underlying storage saturation keeps inflating actual costs and invalidating cost assumptions.

Causal chain: Stale or incomplete statistics mislead the cost model, while independent plan-selection weaknesses (e.g., bind-sensitive caching, version change) choose plans that under-estimate data volume or ignore selective access paths. These sub-optimal plans issue far more I/O than anticipated, quickly pushing the storage layer past its throughput ceiling. The resulting latency amplifies the original costing errors—longer I/O times further distort feedback loops, provoke additional re-compilations, and delay automatic statistics refreshes, which in turn perpetuate inaccurate estimates. Meanwhile, plan instability increases the diversity of I/O patterns (random versus sequential, temp spills), preventing the storage subsystem from stabilizing or caching effectively. The feedback loop between bad estimates, poor plans, and I/O saturation thus reinforces itself, worsening overall performance across both transactional and analytical workloads.

entry.official_definition: Write timeout for X Plugin network communication.
entry.trigger_condition: A MySQL X Protocol write operation exceeds mysqlx_write_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The X Protocol network write operation times out.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL X Plugin system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when network data is not acknowledged, received, or written within the configured transport-level waiting window.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect packet loss, transport latency, client responsiveness, proxy behavior, and whether slow consumers or unstable links are delaying network progress.
